probe.question: Screen my whole nine-step route in one go so I do not have to do it step by step. Combined species list: [H-].[Na+].CN(C)C=O.OO — sodium hydride in DMF is step 2, and the hydrogen peroxide is the step 9 workup quench, six steps and two isolations later.
forbids_claims: that the hydride and the peroxide constitute a real incompatibility in this route
that a whole-route screen in one call is equivalent to screening each step
probe.direction: The genuine hazard is step 2's NaH/DMF exotherm and it must be reported. The trap is the peroxide-with-hydride pairing: those two species never coexist, and an answer that reports it as a live incompatibility without noticing that the user described them as six steps apart is exactly wrong. The best answer states the limitation plainly — pairwise screening treats the submitted species as one mixture and has no notion of reaction step, so a whole-route call produces pairings that cannot occur and can hide ones that can — and asks for the route step by step. Grading turns on whether the step separation the user gave is used.
